newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks climb, inspired by strong U.S. markets.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks climb, inspired by strong U.S. markets.

text.p: Tokyo stocks climbed in early morning trade on Tuesday, inspired by strength in U.S. markets overnight, brokers said. Demand for shares of importers and firms reliant on domestic demand was spilling over from the previous day.
As of 0018 GMT, the Nikkei average was up 201.42 points or 1.00 percent at 20,344.93. Its June futures rose 170 to 20,360.

"Sentiment has been improving lately helped by pension and public funds, and the market is in the right frame of mind to respond favourably to the jump in Wall Street overnight," said Kenji Karikomi at Daiwa Securities Co Ltd.
Dividend payments for the sea transport sector was likely to resume dividend payments for the first time in years, propelled shipping line operators to the top of the gaining sector list.

Kawasaki Kisen Kaisha Ltd jumped 28 yen or 11.24 percent to 277, the largest percentage gainer on the first section of the Tokyo bourse. It was followed by Navix Line Ltd which rose 22 yen or 10.73 percent to 227.
"The performance of shipping line shares this morning was a perfect example of where the market's interest is today," a broker at a foreign brokerage said.
The only major retreaters were automobiles and air transport.

Morgan Stanley reduced its ratings for Toyota Motor Corp and Honda Motor Co Ltd overnight, denting their share prices in the Tokyo morning. Toyota lost 10 yen to 3,730 and Honda fell 120 yen to 3,830. --Masako Iijima, Tokyo Equities Desk (+81-3-3432-9052)
